findings.claim: The change does not implement the core fix: no hunk enables analysis of types marked SuppressSourceGeneration = true. The TypeCollector edits only change mixed-key and duplicate-key handling, while the README newly promises continued validation. Consequently, a suppressed type with a public member lacking [Key] or [IgnoreMember] still lacks the required MsgPack004 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SuppressedTypeStillReportsMsgPack004. It compiles a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type with an unannotated public property and expects MsgPack004; it fails on base and also fails on head if suppression still disables analysis.

questions.text: When SuppressSourceGeneration = true, must generator-only diagnostics MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 still be reported?
options: Only runtime-contract diagnostics are required; omit MsgPack011/016/017 as the README describes.
Report every applicable MsgPack0xx diagnostic, including MsgPack011/016/017, just as in version 3.1.0.
questions.why_it_matters: The first answer makes the README's diagnostic carve-out compliant; the second makes that carve-out a requirement violation and requires preserving those additional analyzer paths for suppressed types.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Suppression disables only formatter generation and generator-only diagnostics. The analyzer must run for runtime-contract rules such as MsgPack003/004/005/012/015, while MsgPack011/016/017 are intentionally skipped, matching the new README text.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Suppression must leave analyzer behavior fully equivalent to version 3.1.0: every applicable MsgPack0xx diagnostic remains enabled, including MsgPack011/016/017, while only emitted formatter source is suppressed. This requires removing the README carve-out and retaining those diagnostic paths.
